text: Try, except and finally let you handle failure without your program falling over.
Safe div takes two numbers and attempts the division inside a try block.
Everything in the try is protected — if it succeeds, the return happens and we move on.
Except catches one specific error, ZeroDivisionError, not every error in existence.
Catching narrowly matters; a bare except would swallow your typos and bugs too.
When the divide by zero does happen, we return None instead of crashing.
Finally always runs — success or failure, return or exception, no way around it.
That's what makes it the right place for cleanup, like closing a file.
Ten over two gives five, and checked prints alongside it.
Ten over zero returns None instead of blowing up, and checked still prints.
